Her Choice. Our Tribute.

A Touch of Fuchsia

Our mother was a firecracker.

Strong-willed, fiercely independent, and never one to shy away from speaking her mind, she knew what she wanted. And if you knew our mother, you knew she wasn't easily persuaded otherwise.

Over the years, conversations about the future would sometimes come up in our family—where Mom might live as she grew older, what mattered most to her, and even the wishes she had for the day we would have to say goodbye.

Those conversations weren't always comfortable. Mom occasionally wondered why anyone was so interested in discussing her final arrangements when she was still very much alive!

But she would engage in the discussion. Her faith was deeply rooted in Christ, and she was at peace with the promise of eternal life. She knew that one day she would be with the Lord. That didn't mean she was in any hurry to leave us!

And when it came to what she wanted, she was perfectly clear.

She wanted to be laid to rest in fuchsia.

Not black. Not white. Fuchsia.

And knowing our mother, that wasn't a suggestion. That was a decision.

Fuchsia is bold, vibrant, and impossible to overlook. In many ways, it reflects the woman we knew and loved: strong, confident, unapologetically herself, and never afraid to stand her ground.

Throughout her celebration, you'll notice subtle touches of fuchsia in the floral arrangements and memorial details. Each is an intentional tribute to her individuality and the wish she shared.

The color was her choice. Honoring it is ours.

A respectful tribute

Attire & Color Guidance

Our immediate family will wear black in honor of Mom, allowing the beautiful fuchsia she selected to remain uniquely hers.

Family and friends are welcome to wear respectful funeral attire, and small touches of fuchsia—a pendant, scarf, flower, or pin—are welcome. We kindly ask guests to avoid fuchsia dresses or predominantly fuchsia outfits, reserving that color as a special tribute to Lynda.

With love and gratitude,
Willie, Ro-Sako, and Almeca
The Children of Lynda Marie Jones

As you make your plans

Guest Information

A few details to help you join us.

Where may I send flowers, cards, or letters?

Address your delivery to Lynda Jones Memorial Service, Embassies of Christ, 4285 Cleveland Street, Gary, IN 46408. View the full mailing information. Please confirm floral receiving instructions before arranging a delivery.

When should I arrive?

Visitation and viewing begin at 10:00 AM CT. The funeral service begins at 11:00 AM CT. Please allow time to arrive and be seated.

What time zone should I use?

All service times are Central Standard Time (CST), the local time in Gary, Indiana. If traveling from another time zone, please adjust your arrival plans accordingly.

What should I wear?

Our immediate family will wear black in honor of Mom. Guests are welcome to wear respectful funeral attire, including small fuchsia accents such as a pendant, scarf, flower, or pin. We kindly ask guests to avoid fuchsia dresses or predominantly fuchsia outfits.

Is the graveside open to everyone?

Yes, to family and friends.

How do I get to the cemetery?

Find the cemetery address and Google Maps or Apple Maps directions in Plan Your Visit.

What should I expect at the cemetery?

The graveside is outdoors in late November. Dress warmly and wear sturdy shoes.
